transcript.text: It’s really good to see you, Tom.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Since I had to give up work, I feel I’m losing touch with my friends and colleagues.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: We really miss you in the office.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: We were all so sorry you had to leave.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: But you must be relieved to have more time to look after your mother.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: How is she?
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Well she is very cheerful, but she needs a lot of help.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Have you tried to get any support from the local council?
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: No, I didn’t know I could.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Yes, they offer different kinds of practical support.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: They realise that carers sometimes need time for all the other responsibilities they have, apart from the person they’re caring for, and also that they sometimes need a break.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Absolutely.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: OK, so tell me more.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: How do I go about getting this support?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Well, you’d have to have an assessment of your mother’s needs.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: That means someone would come round and talk to you about the situation and what you need.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: So, for a start, they’d want to know the amount of time you spend looking after your mother every day.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: OK.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Then they’ll probably ask you what sorts of tasks you do for your mother during the day.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Things like if she needs help with getting dressed, for example.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I help her with that.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: And also I help her get into the shower in the morning.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Yes, that sort of thing.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: They’ll probably ask you if you do the shopping for her and help her at mealtimes, and whether she can cope using money.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Yes, that’s becoming a bit of a problem.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: She used to be very good at it, but not anymore.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: And be ready to tell them about anything you find particularly difficult about caring for your mother.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: So, recently I’ve noticed she’s started to have quite bad problems with her memory.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: If I wasn’t there, I think she’d forget to eat, for example.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: And often she doesn’t seem quite sure what day it is.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Yes, tell them about that.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: And are there any physical difficulties you have caring for her?
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Lifting her, for example?
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Yes, she’s quite heavy and I’m afraid of hurting my back.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I’d be in real trouble if that happened.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: They can give you advice about that and also about how to avoid the possibility of your mum having a fall.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Great.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: So once they’ve done this assessment, if I’m eligible, what happens next?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Well, they might support you financially.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: So they might help you with transport costs, like if you have to get a taxi to take your mother for an appointment, for example.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: I usually drive her myself, actually.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: So, could I claim the petrol?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: You could.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: And you can claim for the insurance too.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Oh, right.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: And if you need help with the housework, they can arrange for someone to come along once or twice a week.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: And one other thing.
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: I hope you don’t mind me saying this, but it's important you look after yourself. And it seems to me you're under quite a bit of stress
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: I am yes
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Well tell the council because they may be able to give you some advice on how to minimise it
transcript.speaker: MAN

transcript.text: Really?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Though, actually, I feel so much better having talked to you.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: I’ll get in touch with the council straight away.
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Now, shall we go for coffee or something?
transcript.speaker: WOMAN

transcript.text: Good morning everyone.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: I’m Steve Wainwright from Elmley Town Council and I organise the town’s volunteer scheme.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: I’m delighted you’re all interested in joining the scheme.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Our volunteers help to create a sense of community among the many people who live in our historic town of Elmley and make residents and visitors feel welcome at local events.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: First, I’ll mention just a few of the activities that volunteers carry out.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: One is to walk around the town centre streets wearing our volunteer T-shirt.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Tourists often ask how to get to a particular shop, and they might also be grateful for recommendations about what to visit.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: The town holds a large number of concerts each year and part of the volunteers’ role is to get everyone in the audience to the right place as smoothly as possible.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: You’d be surprised how many people buy tickets, then don’t check them, and head for the wrong section of the hall.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Volunteers may get involved with community groups, such as sports clubs or gardeners’ associations.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Here, the volunteers talk about how groups can help each other.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: For instance, a writing group might want to travel to another town to hear a talk by a well-known author, but may not know that another club has a coach they could travel in.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: The town produces a monthly magazine, and anyone who lives in the town can send in articles.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: It’s free to residents and is paid for by local businesses.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: That’s the responsibility of the council’s advertising department.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: We depend on volunteers though to find out what people think of events they’ve attended and any suggestions they have for the future.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: The volunteers then send a summary to the editors.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: There are a number of clubs for retired people and every year the council arranges lunch for all the members.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: The volunteers welcome the guests and when everyone’s sitting down and relaxing after the meal, some volunteers put on a show.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Usually around half an hour of songs and short plays, the club members really welcome the chance to chat to the volunteers at these events.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: The town council has a website, of course, and volunteers are asked to help by making sure residents know about it.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: It's updated every day with information about future activities and we want as many people as possible to use it.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: As you probably know, the town arranges three major festivals every year, and they all depend on a large number of volunteers.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: The book festival lasts three days, and uses several venues which all need volunteers.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: More are needed for the music festival because that lasts a whole week, and even more help is required for the science festival, even though it’s only two days long.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: It involves quite a lot of venues, though.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: It’s a good idea to help at the festival you’re most interested in, because you can attend most of the events for free.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: We try to use volunteers who are flexible, though, because some festival events are held outdoors and the weather may affect the size of the audience and even whether the event can take place so there can be changes at short notice What's essential, though, is being able to get on well with other people and also to deal with someone who’s behaving badly, as occasionally happens.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Our plan is to get you all working in September, after a week’s training starting on the 2nd, so we’ll be timetabling you for duties the following week from the 9th onward.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Later in the week beginning September 23rd we have a chat with each of you to find out how you feel about being a volunteer and what extra support you need.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: As a thank you to the volunteers we arrange an annual event.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: In recent years we’ve had a party in the Town Hall and last year a barbecue in Chamber Park.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Our forthcoming event is a trip along the canal from here to Dewhurst and back.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: It’s on Saturday, September the 28th.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: And if you’d like to attend, you can sign up once you start work.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Now, this is the Volunteer’s T-shirt.
transcript.speaker: STEVE

transcript.text: Colin, I’m really struggling to think of a topic for our human geography assignment.

transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: OK.

transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: Lots of facts and statistics.
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: Maybe a bit boring?
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: Yeah, but quite straightforward to find on the internet.

transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: I didn’t get much out of that.

transcript.text: It was all so general and the lecturer didn’t give any useful examples.

transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: We could focus on poverty.
transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: That’s something that’s a global problem.
transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: The trouble is, Dr Lee was saying, that you have to be careful with some of the figures relating to poverty.

transcript.text: They’re sometimes deliberately manipulated.

transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: That sort of thing, yes.

transcript.text: So what are we going to do our assignment on?

transcript.text: I’ll tell you what.
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: One of the possibilities we have discussed is urbanisation and now over half the world population lives in cities.
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: That's really important.
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: OK good idea Rosie Let's do that.
transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: I love living in a big city but of course there are problems
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: Things like theft and robbery?
transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: Yes, but where I come from, that’s linked to another more serious issue, which is that a lot of people don’t have jobs.
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: That’s getting worse and worse.

transcript.text: And we also still have quite a lot of people who are homeless, though that’s not quite so bad as it was.
transcript.speaker: ROSIE

transcript.text: It would be nice to talk about some positive developments, like some of the new developments on the outskirts of cities.
transcript.speaker: COLIN

transcript.text: Yeah, they’ve opened some massive new shopping centres outside my city.

transcript.text: Yeah, the same with mine, but it means a lot of the shops in the city centre are closing down.

transcript.text: But the outskirts are ideal for buildings that need a lot of space, like for conferences.

transcript.text: It’d be nicer to have more facilities for things like football too, but that’s not happening where I live.

transcript.text: There are trends in food much as there are trends in clothing.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Interest in food fashions has risen rapidly since the birth of the smartphone when people first began taking photos of their food and instantly sharing them with their friends.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The food industry in the UK in particular is obsessed with finding and exploiting the next big food trend.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Marketeers aim to create a huge demand for a food item which was previously unknown or not needed.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: One of the most effective ways of promoting a new food product is by using social media influencers as brand ambassadors In return for free samples many influencers will post content about a product although there are influencers with hundreds of thousands of followers who can command large fees for their services Companies which sell vegan produce were pioneers in being able to increase sales really quickly in this way.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: For a food item to become really popular, it has to be readily available.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: So supermarkets have a role to play in creating a new food trend.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: They have dedicated teams closely following which new products or ingredients are trending on social media and are particularly interested in what well-known chefs are putting on their menus.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: I’d like to look at a few examples of marketing campaigns which were really successful in launching a new fashion trend.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Starting in the 1990s with the avocado.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: A British PR company was hired to raise its profile and stimulate demand.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: They paid for a group of journalists to travel out to South Africa to meet avocado farmers.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Articles written following this visit helped to educate the British public about the avocado, which at this time was certainly not the daily staple it’s since become.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Advertisements were designed to promote the avocado as a superfood, rich in nutrients and therefore beneficial for health.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Avocados became hugely fashionable, and within a few years UK avocado sales had grown from £13 million annually to around £150 million, making it one of the most successful fresh produce campaigns in UK history.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Oat milk is a recent example of a new product which became fashionable very quickly.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Now there are many brands available but one company which had early success was the Swedish brand Oatly They attracted a lot of attention with a media campaign which used provocation as a way of getting their message across effectively.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The fact that this campaign aggravated competitors producing milk from dairy cows was seen as a plus, as it helped to make oat milk seem cool.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: In the USA, the brand decided against a big retail launch in favour of getting the product into coffee chains, which removed the need for a big advertising budget.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: This proved far more effective than offering samples in supermarkets.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Oat milk had an advantage over other alternative milk products, such as almond milk.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Many consumers prefer it because it has less of an impact on the environment.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: It requires significantly less water to produce than other alternative milk products and it also has a relatively low carbon footprint.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Norwegian scray, a rarely available seasonal fish delicacy, otherwise known as Arctic cod, is now found on the menus of Michelin-starred restaurants throughout Europe.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The demand for Skre has been used by a food marketing agency to build the reputation of Norway’s fisheries in general.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Marketing surveys have shown that a significant number of shoppers now associate Norway with excellent seafood.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Food trends can be considered a good thing in some ways, as they can benefit farmers and food producers enormously.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: The public can also be encouraged to buy things which are more sustainably produced.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: But ethical concerns have been raised about the effects a surge in demand can cause.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: Quinoa is a classic example.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: This plant is native to Peru and when demand peaked some years ago, the price soared, making it unaffordable for local people.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: While the popularity of quinoa has benefited farmers financially there have been other negative consequences.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: As demand grew, farmers began working the land all year round in order to produce more quinoa.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER

transcript.text: One issue has been that the fertility of the soil decreased dramatically. which could potentially lead to desertification in some areas.
transcript.speaker: LECTURER
